declaration: static iter<T extends RangeValue>(sets: readonly RangeSet<T>[], from: number = 0): RangeCursor<T> {
does: Returns one RangeCursor over all layers of all given sets in order, starting at the first range ending at or after `from` (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:360 (RangeSet^iter)). One LayerCursor per non-empty layer is put in a binary heap ordered by `from`, `startSide`, `rank` (the set's index in `sets`), `to`, `endSide` (:664-667, :683-690, :725-739); the cursor's `rank` reports which set the current range came from.

does: Reports differences between two groups of sets to a RangeComparator, over the parts of the document that `textDiff` leaves unchanged (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:366 (RangeSet^compare)). It drops sets whose top-layer `maxPoint` is not > 0 and which are empty or below `minPointSize` (:376-377), skips Chunk objects shared by both sides at the mapped position and untouched by the diff (findSharedChunks :570-582, only chunks with `maxPoint <= 0`), then for each gap of `textDiff.iterGaps` walks two SpanCursors in step (`compare` :868-896): differing points, or equal points with different active ranges above them, produce `comparePoint` (:880-885); differing active range sets produce `compareRange` (:888); when the comparator has `boundChange`, a span boundary present on only one side, or with a different count of ranges continuing over it, produces `boundChange` at the next non-point span start (:876, :887, :889). Positions are in the new document. An empty diff on an empty document still runs one comparison at 0 (:384).

entry: none: named as not covered by N3 (question Q3)
does: Returns whether two groups of sets are equivalent between `from` (default 0) and `to` (default 1e9 - 1) (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:389 (RangeSet^eq)). Sets present (by identity) in both groups and empty sets are removed first; a different count of remaining sets returns false, none left returns true (:394-397). It then walks two SpanCursors built with minPoint 0 (:399), so LayerCursor.next skips every non-point range (:640) and only point ranges are compared: span ends must match, and points must be equal by `cmpVal` (:401-404). It stops with true after checking the first span ending beyond `to` (:405), so a difference in that span still returns false. A cm6 probe gives true for two sets holding only different non-point ranges (raw/rangeset-questions.jsonl Q22).

does: Walks the spans of a group of sets between `from` and `to`, calling `iterator.span` for stretches not covered by a point and `iterator.point` for each point, and returns the open count at the end (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:415 (RangeSet^spans)). Driven by a SpanCursor (:741-866): active ranges are kept ordered by set rank ascending, then by `to` ascending (addActive :790-799; CHANGELOG 6.4.0); a point hides ranges and points it covers (:832-840) and non-empty points ending exactly at the previous point's end are skipped (:829-831). For a point, `active` holds only active ranges whose set rank is >= the point's rank and that end after the point (or at its end with `endSide >=` the point's) (activeForPoint :850-859) and `openStart` is `active.length + 1` when the point started before `from`, `active.length` when its startSide < 0, else min(active.length, open count) (:428-430); `index` is the point's set rank. With `minPointSize` > -1, only points of at least that size count and non-point ranges are skipped (:640). The return value adds 1 when a point continues past `to` (:437).

does: Moves to the next range (mirrors/cm6/state/src/rangeset.ts:187 (RangeCursor.next)). LayerCursor.next (:627-643) loads the range at the current index and advances the index, crossing chunk boundaries (setRangeIndex :645-656) and, when built with `minPoint >= 0` (internal use only), skipping non-point ranges and smaller points; past the last range it sets `from = to = 1e9` and `value = null`.
